title: DFC, Chubb Announce Additional American Reinsurance Partners and up to $40B in Coverage for Maritime Reinsurance
key_claim: DFC and Chubb announced six additional American reinsurance partners (Travelers, Liberty Mutual, Berkshire Hathaway, AIG, Starr, CNA); $40B rolling facility ($20B from DFC, $20B from Chubb and partners); Chubb is lead underwriter, manages pricing, claims; covers War Hull, War P&I, War Cargo for Hormuz transits.
notes: Primary government source - the operative structure of sovereign reinsurance for a civilian war-risk gap.

publisher: US Federal Register / Department of the Treasury
title: 2026 Report on the Effectiveness of the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program (Notice and request for comment)
key_claim: Treasury and CISA seek public comment (deadline May 8, 2026) on whether cyber incidents are adequately covered under TRIP; Treasury must submit a report to Congress by June 30, 2026 on the overall effectiveness of the program; signals federal consideration of a cyber-insurance backstop.
notes: Primary regulatory source - federal posture on cyber-risk sovereign backstop.

title: How war in the Middle East is turning governments into insurers of last resort
key_claim: Hormuz traffic reduced by ~95%; Joint War Committee of Lloyd's expanded high-risk designation to entire Persian Gulf; ~329 vessels operating in Persian Gulf require ~$352B insurance coverage that private markets no longer provide; WEF analysis projects $0.6T-$5.7T global growth loss from financial-system fragmentation.
notes: Institutional analysis explicitly framing the signal as a structural transformation.

title: Geopolitical Conflict: The role of insurance (systemic risk scenario)
key_claim: Lloyd's-Cambridge model: geopolitical conflict scenario could expose global economy to $7.8T (lowest) to $50T (extreme) five-year losses; baseline modelled at $14.5T; 80%+ of world imports/exports (11Bn tons) at sea at any given time; insurance industry's role is core to economic resilience.
notes: Industry-leader institutional scenario - quantifies the cost of insurability erosion.

title: US Doubles Hormuz Reinsurance Guarantees to $40 Billion With New Partners
key_claim: Insurance industry trade press confirmation of DFC-Chubb $40B facility expansion to six additional American reinsurers; market reaction and operational mechanics.
notes: Industry trade press confirming the DFC announcement and reactions.

title: Maritime War Risk Insurance in the 2026 Iran Crisis
key_claim: War-risk maritime premiums spiked from ~0.25% of vessel value pre-conflict to 3-8% during crisis ($3M-$8M per large tanker transit); Hapag-Lloyd implemented $3,500/container War Risk Surcharge from 02/03/2026; 1,100+ vessels experienced GPS and AIS interference in early conflict phase.
notes: Insurance trade press with pricing-specific quantification anchors.

title: US Treasury Weighs Cyber Insurance Backstop
key_claim: Treasury Federal Register notice (March 2026) re-opens debate on whether catastrophic cyber risk requires a federal backstop similar to TRIP; ransomware, supply-chain, nation-state attacks raise systemic concerns; comment period through May 8, 2026.
notes: Industry coverage of the Treasury TRIP cyber consultation.

title: The DFC maritime reinsurance facility's role with respect to the blockade of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
key_claim: Legal analysis of DFC facility scope and constraints, including questions on extraterritorial coverage of European-flagged tankers carrying crude to China.
notes: Specialist legal analysis surfacing the geopolitical-allocation dynamics.
